name: kv_status
description: [SAFE] Show kv project status. Returns whether a kv project is initialized, the current environment, the number of secrets stored, configured providers, run policy, and the loaded HTTP-policy digest.

name: kv_envs
description: [SAFE] List available environments (e.g. dev, staging, prod). Does not reveal any secret values.

name: kv_list
description: [SAFE] List secret key names in an environment. Returns names only — no secret values are revealed.

name: kv_run
description: [EXECUTE] Run a command with secrets injected as environment variables. Returns exit code and redacted stdout/stderr — the environment's secret values (4 or more characters) and some common encodings of them are replaced with [REDACTED] before the output reaches the AI context (a run with env_names=[] loads no secrets, so nothing is redacted). For a run that receives secrets or a capability, the command is validated against a security policy (allowlist or blocklist) before execution, and shells, inline code, and brokerable network/DB tools are blocked; a run without secrets is checked only for exfiltration patterns. Runs are network-isolated except in three cases: (1) the command matches an entry the owner added with kv network-allow; (2) the run has no vault secrets (env_names=[] and no capability_names); (3) the run uses capability_names. In a protected session, a run with the owner's signed approval gets exactly the network that approval signed, so case 3 alone does not give it the network. Prefer policy-checked kv_api for HTTP work. kv_query and kv_ssh share this execute profile; they are parked on passphrase-protected (v3/v4) vaults, and elsewhere they do not yet have action-level policy. Blocked brokerable commands return broker_handoff guidance with available provider names or setup instructions. When kv_run is necessary, pass env_names with the smallest required secret set; env_names=[] runs without vault secrets. Omitting env_names is blocked for secret-bearing runs because grants must bind to explicit secret names. For brokered HTTP/API work inside a script, pass capability_names with an api:<provider> entry per service so the subprocess receives only a temporary KV_CAP_TOKEN, not the raw provider secret. Capability runs use a private working-directory copy by default; set private_cwd=false only when the user explicitly accepts direct workspace writes. The MCP client SHOULD prompt for user confirmation before calling. Long-running commands are supported.

argv.description: Command and arguments as an array (e.g. ["python", "app.py"])

env_names.description: Explicit secret names to inject. Use [] for no secrets; omit is blocked for secret-bearing runs.

capability_names.description: Broker capabilities to expose through one KV_CAP_TOKEN, api:<provider> only; several services are counted each on its own (the owner approves a count for each). Do not combine with env_names.

cwd.description: Working directory for the command. If omitted, uses the daemon's working directory.

private_cwd.description: Use a private working-directory copy. Defaults on for capability runs; optional for raw secret runs. Set false only for explicit direct-write compatibility.

reason.description: Why this run needs secrets or services, in a short sentence. Recorded in the owner's audit record (and shown with an approval request); never put a secret or key in it.

name: kv_api
description: [SAFE] Make a policy-checked HTTP API call with credentials injected by the kv broker. The API key is held in the daemon (or explicit direct-mode MCP broker) — it never enters your environment, is redacted from tool responses by value matching, and never touches the filesystem. Supports: openai, anthropic, google, github, google-cloud, and custom providers. The agent adds the correct auth header/param automatically. The provider, method, canonical path, query use, and headers must match broker policy; unsafe methods return permit_required without executing. Ask the owner to approve the request, then retry the unchanged call with its permit_id. Returns the API response body (with any secret values redacted).

provider.description: API provider name: openai, anthropic, google, github, google-cloud

method.description: HTTP method (default: GET). Mutating calls require an owner-configured rule and a signed one-call permit for the exact call.

permit_id.description: One-call permit ID from permit_required; retry the exact unchanged call after owner approval.

reason.description: Why this call is needed, in a short sentence. Recorded with a one-call permit in the owner's audit record; never put a secret or key in it.

body.description: Request body (JSON). Omit for GET requests.

headers.description: Extra headers to include (auth headers are added automatically).

name: kv_query
description: [EXECUTE] Run an arbitrary database/Redis operation with credentials injected by the kv broker. Parked on passphrase-protected (v3/v4) vaults, the kind kv init makes, in this release (not offered there). The database password is held in the daemon (or explicit direct-mode MCP broker) — it never enters your environment. Supports PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Redis providers configured via 'kv provider add'. Action-level SQL/Redis policy is not implemented, so this tool is opt-in. Returns query results with any secret values redacted. For HTTP API calls, use kv_api instead.

provider.description: Database provider name (configured via kv provider add --type postgres/mysql/redis)

query.description: SQL query (Postgres/MySQL) or Redis command to execute

name: kv_ssh
description: [EXECUTE] Run an arbitrary command on a remote server via SSH with credentials injected by the kv broker. Parked on passphrase-protected (v3/v4) vaults, the kind kv init makes, in this release (not offered there). The SSH key or password is held in the daemon (or explicit direct-mode MCP broker) — it never enters your environment. Configure SSH providers via 'kv provider add --type ssh'. Remote-command action policy is not implemented, so this tool is opt-in. Returns stdout, stderr, and exit code with any secret values redacted.

provider.description: SSH provider name (configured via kv provider add --type ssh)

command.description: Command to execute on the remote server

name: kv_set
description: [MUTATE] [DIRECT ONLY] Store or update an encrypted secret. Requires explicit direct vault access while the daemon is stopped, which passphrase-protected (v3/v4) vaults refuse (not offered there); prefer the CLI. The value is encrypted immediately using ChaCha20-Poly1305. The MCP client SHOULD prompt for user confirmation before calling.

name: kv_rm
description: [MUTATE] [DIRECT ONLY] Remove a secret from the encrypted store. Requires explicit direct vault access while the daemon is stopped, which passphrase-protected (v3/v4) vaults refuse (not offered there); prefer the CLI. This action is irreversible. The MCP client SHOULD prompt for user confirmation before calling.

name: kv_get
description: [REVEAL] [DIRECT ONLY] Get a secret value by name. Requires explicit direct vault access while the daemon is stopped, which passphrase-protected (v3/v4) vaults refuse (not offered there); prefer the CLI. WARNING: The decrypted value is returned in plaintext to the AI context. This means the secret will be visible to the language model. Prefer kv_run to use secrets without revealing them. The MCP client SHOULD prompt for user confirmation before calling.
